text:
alex: Hey team — we need to open Azure quota + capacity reservation requests for an upcoming Dedicated cluster launch. Target regions: westeurope (primary) and northeurope (failover). Date window: provisioning week of 2026-03-30.

alex: Details: subscription ID 3f8a2b7c-XXXX-4d2a-9f1b-abcdef123456 (redacted here). Workload requires the following steady-state capacity: ~12 x Standard_ND96asr_v4 in westeurope for low-latency inference + burst pool of 8 x Standard_NC24ads_A100 for large-batch jobs. Also need increasing regional GPU core quota for the ND/NC families while we request a reservation or capacity hold.

maria: @cloud-ops can you triage whether we should request a quota increase only or also ask Azure for a capacity reservation (capacity reservation is higher effort but gives stronger guarantees)? We will likely sign a Reserved Capacity agreement if they require it.

cloud-ops: We should do both: quota increase + a capacity reservation request. I've seen westeurope be tight for ND96 last quarter. I'll open the SR with Microsoft once we have exact SKU counts per region and the business justification. Also need the billing/contact PO and cost center string.

alex: Cost center: ENG-INFRA-DED and AR code 22-IF-0126. Business justification: "Production inference fleet for Redwood Dedicated customers — latency SLOs and capacity isolation. Peak steady tokens/sec require pinned A100 capacity to avoid throttling and cold-start delays."

chris: FYI, I ran the usage check earlier. Output for westeurope:

```
az vm list-usage --location westeurope --output table
Name                                     CurrentValue  Limit
Standard ND family vCPUs                 84            100
Standard NC family vCPUs                 40            50
```

chris: That means we still need +28 vCPU quota for ND-family and +32 vCPU for NC-family in westeurope if each ND96 counts as 8 vCPU-per-GPU (Azure reporting is weird). Recommend asking for +60 vCPUs on ND family to be safe.

cloud-ops: Good catch. For the SR I need: exact SKU list, counts per SKU per region, subscription ID, cost center, and target provisioning date. Also any preferred Azure account rep / tenant contact if you have one.

alex: SKU list: westeurope: 12x Standard_ND96asr_v4; 6x Standard_NC24ads_A100 (burst pool). northeurope: 4x Standard_ND96asr_v4 for failover. Please request quota increases for ND/NC families and ask for a capacity hold for the 12 ND96asr_v4 in westeurope (start 2026-03-30, 6-month window with option to extend).

maria: Adding context for the SR notes: "Customer: Redwood Inference (internal). Use-case: Dedicated inference serving for enterprise customers. SLA requires <80ms p99 token latency under steady load. Without reservation we observed preemption/placement delays in previous launches. Requesting short-term capacity hold and quota bump to cover initial launch and cold-start buffer."

cloud-ops: Opening SR now. Draft SR description:

```
We are requesting a quota increase and capacity reservation for GPU SKUs in westeurope and northeurope for subscription 3f8a2b7c-XXXX-4d2a-9f1b-abcdef123456. Requested: 12x Standard_ND96asr_v4 (westeurope) + 6x Standard_NC24ads_A100 (westeurope), 4x Standard_ND96asr_v4 (northeurope). Please increase ND-family vCPU quota by 60 and NC-family vCPU quota by 40 in westeurope. Request capacity reservation (hold) for 12 ND96asr_v4 in westeurope starting 2026-03-30 for 6 months. Business justification: Production inference fleet for Redwood Dedicated customers — latency SLOs and capacity isolation. Contact: alex@redwood.example / +1-555-0102. Cost center: ENG-INFRA-DED.
```

cloud-ops: Submitted SR# 20260318-84721 to Microsoft support. ETA for initial response: 24-48h. I've flagged it as "quota & capacity" escalate. Adding Azure rep cc.

infra-bot: Support ticket created: SR#20260318-84721. Status: New. Assigned: Microsoft GPU-Quota Team.

maria: Thanks. Can someone paste the portal link or SR link once the rep responds? Also we should prepare a fallback plan: if reservation isn't approved, can we spread to eastus2 as contingency?

chris: Eastus2 check: availability looks OK but would increase latency for EU customers. If needed we can deploy a smaller fleet there for spillover; will require updated routing policies in smart-routing layer. Cost estimate for eastus2 burst: +~25% network egress.

alex: Noted. Priority is keeping primary in westeurope. Please add me and maria to SR watchers. Also tagging @cloud-ops for weekly follow-ups until resolved.

cloud-ops: Added watchers. I'll post MS updates here. Next steps: wait for Azure reply, supply any additional info they request (topology diagrams, peak RPS/requests per second, expected token throughput).

infra-bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up in 48h (2026-03-20 09:30 UTC).

chris: If MS asks for deployment diagram, here's a tiny ascii sketch to paste: 

```
[westeurope - reserved ND96 x12] -> load-balancer -> inference pool (k8s nodes)
[northeurope - failover ND96 x4] -> load-balancer -> fallback pool
[burst (westeurope) NC24 x6] -> batch jobs queue
```

alex: Perfect. I'll prepare the service-level notes for the SR (SLA, expected throughput numbers) and upload to the SR thread when ready. Thanks all.

cloud-ops: Closing interim: SR open, watchers set, follow-up scheduled. Will post ticket URL once Microsoft assigns a rep."
